comparison: Perfect agreement on model limitations (C86, C87). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers acknowledge the authors' appropriate recognition that the acute sepsis model has temporal and complexity limitations compared to clinical sepsis.

Strong agreement on coagulation findings (C5, C6, C8, C23, C24, C32-C34). Both evaluations find the data well-supported. OpenEval also includes C31, C88 and survival data (C47-C49) which peer reviewers also accept. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on glycine protection data (C7, C9, C26, C73-C77, C82). Both find the pharmacological validation compelling and rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval includes C72 and notes the MV count discrepancy, while peer reviewers focus on therapeutic potential (C80).

Agreement on E. coli infection model findings (C51-C53, C55, C57). Both evaluations find this data confirmatory and well-supported. OpenEval includes additional claims (C54, C56) about the translational relevance. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Agreement on therapeutic potential (C84, C85). Both appropriately frame this as speculative future potential. OpenEval also includes C83 (synthesis of findings) and C86-C87. Both rate as SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats.

Agreement on uncertainty regarding MV count discrepancy (C78, C79). Both note the unexplained difference between in vitro and in vivo results and the speculative nature of the authors' explanation. Both rate as UNCERTAIN.

Partial agreement on cytokine findings (C25, C35, C43). Both note mechanistic uncertainty. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED despite incomplete mechanistic understanding, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting clarification on IL-1β release discrepancies. OpenEval includes additional mechanistic claims (C36-C40).

Disagreement on heterozygous mouse model justification (C27, C88). OpenEval finds the use of Ninj1+/- mice well-justified and rates as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, calling it 'a critical limitation' and recommending cell line validation.

Divergent evaluations of PMR and MV data. OpenEval (R5) focuses on PMR-cell death dissociation (C59-C62, C68-C69) and rates as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers (R4) focus on MV characterization concerns (C63-C67) and rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting additional validation (EM, NTA, functional assays).

OpenEval finds NINJ1 in MVs and correlation data (C23, C63-C67) well-supported. Peer reviewers express concerns about Figure 3A protein expression patterns and request additional MV characterization and functional validation. OpenEval rates SUPPORTED, peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN.

Both address overlapping claims about tissue damage and survival (C8, C47-C49). OpenEval focuses specifically on fibrin immunostaining limitations (C45-C46) and immunoblot validation, rating as SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers incorporate these into broader acceptance of coagulation findings.

Both address fibrin detection (C45, C46). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, acknowledging technical limitations but accepting immunoblot validation. Peer reviewers also accept this data without concerns (R9), treating it as methodologically sound.

Agreement on pyroptosis model validation (C89, C28). Both find the experimental validation of caspase-1 activation, IL-1β processing, GSDMD cleavage, and LDH release appropriate. Both rate as SUPPORTED.

Both address GSDMD control data (C39). OpenEval includes this as part of broader cytokine analysis showing NINJ1 reduction doesn't affect GSDMD levels. Peer reviewers treat this as accepted methodological control. Both implicitly support this finding.

OpenEval identifies C70 (cell repair hypothesis) as purely speculative with no experimental evidence, rating as UNCERTAIN. No corresponding peer review evaluation found addressing this specific claim.

OpenEval evaluates extensive background literature claims (C1-C3, C10-C22, C29-C30, C41-C42, C44, C50, C58, C71) as SUPPORTED, noting they provide necessary context from prior work. Peer reviewers do not separately evaluate these background claims.
